edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), Ad martyres, via Latin Wikisource transcription

source_text: Inter carnis alimenta, benedicti martyres designati, quae vobis et domina mater Ecclesia de uberibus suis, et singuli fratres de opibus suis propriis in carcerem subministrant, capite aliquid et a nobis quod faciat ad spiritum quoque educandum. Carnem enim saginari, et spiritum esurire non prodest. Imo, si quod infirmum est, curatur; aeque, quod infirmius est, negligi non debet. Nec tantus ego sum, ut vos alloquar; verumtamen et gladiatores perfectissimos non tantum magistri et praepositi sui, sed etiam idiotae et supervacui quique adhortantur de longinquo, ut saepe de ipso populo dictata suggesta profuerint. In primis ergo, benedicti, nolite contristare Spiritum sanctum, qui vobiscum introiit carcerem. Si enim non vobiscum nunc introisset, nec vos illic hodie fuissetis. Et ideo date operam, ut illic vobiscum perseveret: ita vos inde perducat ad Dominum. Domus quidem diaboli est et carcer, in qua familiam suam continet. Sed vos ideo in carcerem pervenistis, ut illum etiam in domo sua conculcetis. Jam enim foris congressi conculcaveratis. Non ergo dicat: In meo sunt, tentabo illos vilibus scidiis, affectionibus, aut inter se dissensionibus. Fugiat conspectum vestrum, et ima sua delitescat contractus et torpens, tanquam coluber excantatus aut effumigatus. Nec illi tam bene sit in suo regno, ut vos committat sed inveniat munitos, et concordia armatos: quia pax vestra bellum est illi. Quam pacem quidam in Ecclesia non habentes, a martyribus in carcere exorare consueverunt. Et ideo eam etiam propterea in vobis habere et fovere et custodire debetis, ut si forte et aliis praestare possitis.
pass_a_gloss: Among the nourishments of the flesh, blessed designated martyrs, which are supplied to you both by the Lady Mother Church from her own breasts and by individual brothers from their own resources into prison, let us also contribute something from our side towards the nourishment of the spirit. For it is not beneficial to fatten the flesh and starve the spirit. Indeed, if something weak is being cured, equally something weaker ought not to be neglected. Nor am I so great that I should address you; nevertheless, even the most perfect gladiators are not only exhorted by their own masters and superiors but also by private individuals and any idle person from a distance, so that often suggestions dictated by the crowd themselves have been of use. First of all, therefore, blessed ones, do not grieve the Holy Spirit who entered prison with you. For if he had not entered with you now, you would not be there today. And therefore, take care that he perseveres with you there, so that he may lead you through to the Lord. The prison is indeed the house of the devil and a place where he keeps his family. But you have arrived in prison so that you may also trample him in his own house. For you have already trampled him outside. Let him not say: They are in my domain, I will test them with vile temptations, affections, or dissensions among themselves. Let him flee from your sight and hide his lowest parts, contracted and numb, like a snake that has been charmed or smoked out. Nor let him be so comfortable in his kingdom that he may hand you over, but let him find you fortified and armed with harmony, because your peace is war to him. This peace, which some do not have in the Church, they are accustomed to beg from martyrs in prison. And therefore, you ought to have, nurture, and guard this peace, so that if perhaps you may be able to provide it to others as well.
pass_b_english: Among the physical rations supplied to you, blessed martyrs-designate — rations sent by our Lady Mother Church from her own breasts and by individual brothers from their own resources — let us also contribute something to nourish the spirit. Fattening the flesh while starving the spirit helps nothing. Indeed, if something weak is being cured, the weaker thing must not be neglected. I am not great enough to address you, yet even the most perfect gladiators are exhorted not only by their own trainers and superiors but also by private citizens and idle onlookers from a distance; often the shouted suggestions of the crowd itself have proved useful. First of all, then, blessed ones, do not grieve the Holy Spirit who entered prison with you. If he had not entered with you now, you would not be there today. So take care that he perseveres with you there, so that he may lead you through to the Lord. The prison is indeed the devil's house, where he keeps his family. But you have arrived in prison precisely to trample him in his own house, since you have already trampled him outside. Let him not say: 'They are in my domain; I will test them with vile temptations, lusts, or dissensions among themselves.' Let him flee your sight and hide his lowest parts, contracted and numb, like a snake that has been charmed or smoked out. Nor let him be so comfortable in his kingdom that he can hand you over; let him find you fortified and armed with harmony, because your peace is war to him. Some who lack this peace in the Church are accustomed to beg it from martyrs in prison. And therefore you ought to have, nurture, and guard this peace, so that if perhaps you may be able to provide it to others as well.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'idiotae' as 'private individuals' (A) and 'private citizens' (B) is a valid interpretation of the Latin sense in this context, as noted in the lemmas. All clauses, including the complex comparison to gladiators and the description of the devil's reaction, are preserved.
